title: Upstash MCP Server
summary: Use Upstash's hosted MCP server to manage Redis databases, QStash and Workflow from your coding agent with OAuth sign-in and no local install.
description: Upstash offers a remote MCP server that exposes its serverless products to an agent: Redis databases, QStash messaging, Workflow, Vector, Search and Blob. The older npm package is no longer maintained, so this setup uses the hosted URL.

Sign-in is OAuth in the browser. For a headless machine, Upstash accepts a Basic authorization header built from your email and API key instead. A read-only API key turns off every tool that changes state.
useWhen: Spin up a free Redis database for a prototype
Run a Redis command against a staging database
List QStash schedules that are failing
Audit which Upstash databases an account has

mcp.name: upstash
access: Upstash databases and queues on the account you sign in with
Can create and delete databases unless you sign in with a read-only API key

example.prompt: Which of my Upstash Redis databases is the largest, and what region is it in?
example.result: cache-prod is the largest at 412 MB, in eu-west-1. The next is jobs-queue at 96 MB in us-east-1.

faq.question: Can I keep it read-only?
faq.answer: Yes. Upstash supports read-only API keys, and with one the server disables all tools that modify state.

faq.question: What about CI or servers without a browser?
faq.answer: Send an Authorization header of the form Basic base64(email:api_key) instead of using OAuth. Keep that value out of the repo.

access: Reads and manages Upstash resources on your account
Runs Redis commands on databases you choose
